observations.title: A normative field makes a false statement about the document's own text
observations.detail: $.t1CancellationComposition.composition.onHostObservedProcessDeath ends 'The phrase cancellation-equivalent is not used.' The phrase in fact occurs on three lines of v3 (this sentence, reviewGuidance, and honestyRepairsFromV2). All three are mentions, not uses: none functions as a trigger, so the substantive repair is genuine. Still, a normative field asserting something demonstrably false about its own bytes is the kind of claim a later reviewer will trip over. Suggest 'cancellation-equivalent is not a trigger in this contract.'

observations.title: Codex finding ids are written two different ways inside one artifact
observations.detail: appliesFindingsOf.idCollisionNote and codexv2.blockers declare CSCV2-B1 / CSCV2-B2, and basedOn.method repeats 'Codex CSCV2-B1/B2'. But honestyRepairsFromV2 refers to 'CODEX-V2-B2' and 'CODEX-V2-B1'. The idCollisionNote field exists precisely to keep finding ids reconcilable, and the repairs list then uses a different prefix. Cosmetic, but the coordinator reconciles repairs to findings by id. (Inherited pattern: v2 did the same with CSCV1-* vs CODEX-V1-*.)

observations.title: The eligibility sampler is not named, though the lawful reading is determinate
observations.detail: $.composition.hostEventTransitionRelation.sampleEligibilityAt tests 'the applied provider contract's admissible causes and current state' without naming which participant performs the test. Provider protocol state is not control-plane-visible under CPC v2's opacity rule (content invisible; 'recognizing [a provider duplicate] would require reading content'), so a control-plane-side test would be unlawful. $.split.providerInBandCancel already assigns that frame 'wholly' to the host's provider-side participant, which makes the lawful reading the only coherent one. Not filed as a finding because no source is contradicted; naming the participant would close the last ambiguity.

CLAUDE-V2-B1 REPAIRED — the J-1 translation exception is gone. Both surviving occurrences of 'except' in the T-1 block are negations: j1 now reads 'J-1 does not grant the control plane a translation exception' and mustNot reads 'No exception.' The new j1 text matches CPC v2's J-1 rule ('the owning contract then decides what a result-after-cancel or cancel-after-result IS') and ID-DEP-2 ('the J-1..J-5 orderings bind ORDERING and refusal-class identity only').

The B1 opacity defect is also repaired: noFanoutWhen is now stated from the provider contract's side ('remains wholly within the provider contract and never creates CPC supervision meaning') and no longer directs control-plane behaviour upon a provider frame the control plane may not recognize.

CLAUDE-V2-SF1 REPAIRED — the invented trigger is gone. 'cancellation-equivalent' no longer appears as a normative trigger anywhere (three residual occurrences are all mentions). onHostObservedProcessDeath now states death is teardown-only, and its stated reason ('the provider transition is unavailable from a terminal state') matches delivery.v2's cancelTransition verbatim in substance: 'Cancel may be sent once from any nonterminal state'. CPC v2 likewise places process death at T-5 of the teardown ladder.

The remaining two fanout triggers are correctly guarded by the applied contract's admissible causes. delivery.v2's CancelV1.reason is the closed enum 'user-interrupt|host-shutdown'; item 1 covers exactly those, and item 2 (deadline expiry) carries its own 'only if currently admissible' guard in the item itself rather than in a distant rule. This is a real structural improvement over v2, where the guard sat in a separate field.

The new sequencing is consistent with both governing contracts: 'Commit the provider-side in-band Cancel FIRST. Then emit CPC supervision teardown' matches delivery.v2's userCancellation ordering ('send Cancel once, close the request side, allow the host's bounded cleanup grace, then terminate the child if needed') and sits cleanly ahead of CPC v2's teardown ladder T-1..T-5. ifNotAdmissible ('Do not invent a provider Cancel') preserves the non-authoring rule.

Closed roster holds everywhere except the one key at CLAUDE-V3-SF1: t1CancellationComposition changed ONLY at /composition as scoped, no keys were removed, reviewGuidance is a PURE APPEND (first 11 items identical), and all other off-roster keys are byte-identical to v2.

summary: Substantively this is the strongest version so far, and both of my v2 findings are genuinely repaired rather than papered over. The J-1 translation exception is deleted and replaced with language that matches CPC v2's J-1 rule and ID-DEP-2; the invented cancellation-equivalent trigger is gone and death is now teardown-only for a reason that matches delivery.v2's nonterminal-state rule word for word; and the fanout is now a sequenced transition relation whose ordering matches the applied contract's own cancel-then-terminate sequence, with both surviving triggers guarded in-place by admissible causes. The carried text remains byte-exact and no v1 repair regressed. One defect stops it: reMeasurementAtV3 is a new top-level key that the declared closed roster does not list, and the immediate predecessor DID list its equivalent - so the artifact fails the exact silent-path test its own reviewGuidance sets. The key's contents are truthful and I verified them live, which is why this is a SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker. It is a one-line fix to the roster string.
